source_policy: Only original research papers, original-author book material, and official NASA/MIT/CMU/Cornell/author sources are used for technical support. Secondary search results were not used as authority.
omission_claim_boundary: Confirmed: none of the eight candidates is a standalone option in the inspected hosted evaluator enum. Unknown: whether a broader archival method definition, alias, or unretrieved implementation already covers the concept. Current exposure limits are compared explicitly.

sources.title: Linearizability: A Correctness Condition for Concurrent Objects
sources.author_or_owner: Maurice Herlihy and Jeannette Wing; author-hosted original paper
sources.retrieval: Original PDF opened with parsed text; definition located.
sources.locator: Definition of linearizability: legal sequential history and real-time ordering.
sources.supports: An object history must admit a legal sequential explanation consistent with non-overlap ordering, with pending operations handled under the chosen definition.

sources.title: Weak Consistency: A Generalized Theory and Optimistic Implementations for Distributed Transactions
sources.author_or_owner: Atul Adya; MIT original dissertation, MIT-LCS-TR-786
sources.retrieval: Original MIT PDF opened with parsed text.
sources.locator: Chapter 3 dependency definitions and serialization graphs; Chapter 4 isolation distinctions.
sources.supports: Transaction dependencies and prohibited graph structures express isolation guarantees; the edge meanings and history completeness matter.

sources.title: Counterexample-Guided Abstraction Refinement for Symbolic Model Checking
sources.author_or_owner: Clarke and coauthors; original paper on the CMU author archive
sources.retrieval: Original author-hosted PDF opened with parsed text.
sources.locator: Abstraction, model checking, counterexample analysis, and refinement loop.
sources.supports: An abstract counterexample must be checked for concrete feasibility; a spurious path refines the abstraction rather than becoming a system defect.

sources.title: Simplifying and Isolating Failure-Inducing Input
sources.author_or_owner: Andreas Zeller and Ralf Hildebrandt; original research paper hosted by Purdue
sources.retrieval: Original paper PDF opened with parsed prose; some mathematical glyphs have extraction artifacts.
sources.supports: Oracle-driven subset/complement trials reduce failure-inducing input; one-element minimality is different from global minimum size.

sources.title: Learning Assumptions for Compositional Verification
sources.author_or_owner: Cobleigh, Giannakopoulou and Pasareanu; original paper in NASA NTRS
sources.retrieval: Original NASA-hosted PDF opened with parsed text.
sources.locator: Assume-guarantee rule and learned assumption automata; the stated rule is asymmetric and noncircular.
sources.supports: Checking a component under an assumption is insufficient unless the other component satisfies that assumption under the chosen composition rule.

sources.title: Hyperproperties
sources.author_or_owner: Michael Clarkson and Fred Schneider; original paper on Cornell author site
sources.retrieval: Original author-hosted PDF opened with parsed text.
sources.locator: Information-flow examples and discussion of relations among executions/self-composition.
sources.supports: Some security policies concern sets or relations of traces, so accepting individual traces does not establish those policies.

sources.title: Probabilistic Risk Assessment Procedures Guide for NASA Managers and Practitioners, Second Edition
sources.retrieval: Official NASA PDF opened with parsed text.
sources.locator: Section 3.3.2, event sequence diagrams/event trees; Chapter 7, dependent and common-cause events.
sources.supports: Initiating events branch through consequential events; dependencies must be modeled rather than assumed independent. Numeric risk requires an independently supported probability model.

sources.title: Algorithmic Mechanism Design
sources.author_or_owner: Noam Nisan and Amir Ronen; original paper reproduced in Ronen dissertation
sources.retrieval: Original author dissertation opened with parsed text; Chapter 2 identifies the reproduced original paper.
sources.locator: Chapter 2, mechanism definition and dominant-strategy implementation.
sources.supports: A mechanism specifies outcomes and payments from reports; incentive compatibility compares truthful utility with utility under alternative reports.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach — Logical Agents
sources.author_or_owner: Stuart Russell and Peter Norvig; official book website
sources.retrieval: Author-provided chapter opened with parsed text.
sources.supports: Finite truth-assignment enumeration checks whether every model satisfying a propositional knowledge base also satisfies a query.

sources.title: Specifying Systems
sources.retrieval: Author-provided PDF opened with parsed text.
sources.locator: Invariant/inductive invariant discussion and specification/refinement chapters; search for inductive invariant.
sources.supports: Initial-state and transition-preservation obligations justify invariance relative to a specification. A refinement relation needs explicit proof obligations, not similar labels or traces.

sources.title: Diagnostic Expert Systems Based on a Set Covering Model
sources.author_or_owner: James Reggia, Dana Nau and Pearl Wang; original author-hosted paper
sources.retrieval: Original PDF opened, but parsed text length was zero. Primary search excerpt verified a set-cover hypothesize-and-test mechanism. Tavily basic extraction failed. Fine-grained implementation equivalence was not verified.
sources.locator: Paper title/primary indexed abstract; detailed local set-cover semantics below are an explicit adaptation.
sources.supports: Diagnostic hypotheses can be organized through a set-cover model. This source does not certify the proposed bounded cover implementation.

sources.title: Abductive Logic Programming
sources.author_or_owner: Kakas, Kowalski and Toni; original authors, Imperial College archive
sources.retrieval: Original PDF opened; parsed text has substantial character-encoding artifacts. Broad framework confirmed by primary indexed description; no claim of reproducing its proof procedure.
sources.locator: Abduction, background theory, abducibles and integrity constraints.
sources.supports: Abduction forms constrained explanatory hypotheses. Covering a supplied observation set is a narrower operation than general abductive logic programming.

sources.title: Model-Based Safety Analysis
sources.retrieval: Official NASA-hosted PDF opened with parsed text.
sources.locator: PDF page 45 discussion of extracting minimal sets of basic events producing a top-level event.
sources.supports: Minimal cut sets identify minimally sufficient basic-event combinations in a model. The proposed AND/OR evaluator is a finite qualitative subset, not the publication's complete analysis system.

sources.title: A Revised and Verified Proof of the Scalable Commutativity Rule
sources.source_kind: Original research, MIT CSAIL and Harvard authors; hosted by MIT CSAIL
sources.representation: Parsed text of the 9-page primary PDF
sources.source_claim_scope: Defines state-dependent, interface-based and monotonic commutativity. Records a flaw in the original proof and a revised proof. Distinguishes a specification's allowed histories from the subset a reference implementation exhibits.
sources.limitation: Neither the paper's existence nor its verified theorem establishes commutativity, correctness or scalability of the user's system.

sources.title: The Scalable Commutativity Rule: Designing Scalable Software for Multicore Processors
sources.inspected_location: Primary thesis opened; use revised proof source for the precise theorem and correction
sources.representation: Parsed text of the 95-page primary PDF
sources.source_claim_scope: Original method lineage for interface-model commutativity and Commuter.
sources.limitation: The older proof must not be cited without the recorded later correction.

sources.title: Knowledge and Common Knowledge in a Distributed Environment
sources.source_kind: Original 1990 Journal of the ACM paper, university-hosted copy
sources.inspected_location: Section 6 view-based interpretations, journal pages 559-563 / PDF pages 11-15
sources.representation: Readable parsed text of the 39-page MIT-hosted primary PDF
sources.source_claim_scope: Knowledge holds when a proposition is true at every point with the same agent view. Group distributed knowledge uses joint views; common knowledge uses reachability through the group's indistinguishability edges.
sources.limitation: The Cornell copy opened but yielded garbled text; detailed verification used the readable MIT copy. This is information-theoretic knowledge relative to a model, not a claim about human awareness or an agent's computational ability.

hooks.name: Linearizability checking of object histories
hooks.mechanism: Search for a sequential ordering that respects known real-time precedence and the object's declared sequential specification. Each operation must have a legal placement; missing/pending operations need explicit treatment.
proposed_input_contract: Source-bound operation IDs, actor/client IDs and object identities
Invocation/response boundaries and observed results
Known ordering relations with clock uncertainty recorded
Initial object state and exact sequential specification
Pending-operation policy and finite search budget
hooks.exposure_comparison: No standalone evaluator is exposed. partial_order explicitly checks one supplied complete order; it does not generate schedules or check whether a legal linearization exists.
hooks.implementation_route: Add a separate bounded offline history checker that explores admissible orders and calls a pure sequential transition function. Return a legal witness, exhausted bounded counterexample, or inconclusive budget/incomplete-history result. Do not generate target traffic.
focused_acceptance_cases: Two overlapping operations with a valid order produce that witness
Two successful removals from one modeled token are rejected under the one-token specification
Unknown invocation boundaries or exhausted search budget stay inconclusive
hooks.falsifier_or_model_defeater: A legal sequential witness defeats the claim for this modeled history. An incomplete trace, wrong specification, or unjustified clock order defeats the applicability of the conclusion.
limits: Linearizability is appropriate only when that consistency contract is required
Finite history checking does not prove correctness of all executions
A modeled violation does not establish native exploitation or money loss

hooks.name: Transaction dependency and serializability analysis
hooks.mechanism: Construct transaction dependencies from explicit reads, writes, versions and predicates, then check the prohibited cycles for the declared isolation criterion. Transaction-level constraints differ from ordering individual object operations.
proposed_input_contract: Committed/aborted/pending transaction identities and boundaries
Read-from and write-version relations with provenance
Predicate-read coverage where applicable
Declared isolation/serializability criterion
Complete dependency domain or explicit missing-edge state
hooks.exposure_comparison: No transaction-isolation evaluator is exposed. A generic cycle check in partial_order does not supply transactional edge semantics, read dependencies, or an isolation model.
hooks.implementation_route: Implement a typed dependency-graph adapter and a finite cycle/witness routine. Reuse identity validation, but classify edges by the selected formal model. Return the transaction/edge witness and the exact criterion violated.
focused_acceptance_cases: A serial schedule is accepted under its declared criterion
A fully specified write-skew fixture produces its relevant dependency cycle
Omitted read-from/predicate evidence prevents a completeness claim
hooks.falsifier_or_model_defeater: If an alleged edge is not a committed dependency, or the selected model permits it, the claimed anomaly fails. Acyclic observed fragments do not prove an incomplete history serializable.
limits: API response order is not an observed database transaction history
Conflict, multiversion, strict and other serializability notions must not be interchanged
A cycle matters only under the chosen edge definitions and criterion

hooks.name: Counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (CEGAR)
hooks.mechanism: Build an abstraction, check a declared property, and test any abstract counterexample for feasibility in the concrete model. Refine the abstraction when the path is spurious; preserve a concrete model witness when it is feasible.
proposed_input_contract: Concrete transition model and property
Abstraction mapping/predicates with version
Soundness or over-approximation obligation
Counterexample feasibility checker
Refinement rule and explicit state/time/iteration bounds
hooks.exposure_comparison: No CEGAR/model-checking evaluator is exposed. refine_counterexample triages caller-supplied PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN checks; state_trace explicitly excludes exhaustive state-space proof.
hooks.implementation_route: Start with an explicit finite-state adapter outside the hosted enum. Record each abstraction version, feasibility result, refinement and termination reason. A later solver integration must declare its actual semantics and limits.
focused_acceptance_cases: A deliberately coarse abstraction creates a spurious path that refinement removes
A feasible violating path survives concretization
Unsound abstraction or budget exhaustion never returns global VERIFIED
hooks.falsifier_or_model_defeater: Failure to concretize an abstract path defeats its promotion as a concrete defect. A new reachable transition outside the model defeats an unqualified real-system conclusion.
limits: Not an Alloy/SAT/SMT solver merely because it uses abstraction language
Termination and coverage depend on the declared model and procedure
Counterexample feasibility in a model is not observed target behavior

hooks.name: Oracle-driven delta debugging and witness minimization
hooks.mechanism: Use a reproducible oracle to test subsets and complements of a failure-inducing configuration. Retain smaller failing configurations and determine the declared form of minimality; unresolved tests are not successful removals.
proposed_input_contract: Original immutable failing fixture/trace and hash
Explicit removable units and dependency constraints
PASS/FAIL/UNRESOLVED oracle with stable failure signature
Reset/isolation procedure
Budget and chosen minimality definition
hooks.exposure_comparison: No minimizer is exposed. refine_counterexample does not run an oracle; delta_plan computes changed-node dependency closure and is not delta debugging.
hooks.implementation_route: Run a bounded local ddmin-style adapter on synthetic fixtures or already authorized reproducible local records. Preserve derivation links to the original. Use the existing one-variable comparator only for suitable final single-removal checks, not arbitrary multi-unit reductions.
focused_acceptance_cases: Irrelevant fixture units are removed while the exact failure signature persists
Invalid reduced configurations return UNRESOLVED
All one-unit removals are checked before claiming 1-minimality
hooks.falsifier_or_model_defeater: A remaining unit removable without changing the failure defeats a 1-minimal claim. A flaky/different failure signature defeats the causal interpretation of the reduction.
limits: 1-minimal is not globally minimum or a proved root cause
It must not become an unauthorized automated target tester
Deleting source evidence does not simplify the original; only a linked derivative is reduced

hooks.name: Assume-guarantee reasoning across components
hooks.mechanism: Check a component's property under an explicit environment assumption and separately check that the composing environment satisfies the assumption. Use a sound composition rule rather than joining independent component passes.
proposed_input_contract: Component transition models and interface alphabets
Property and explicit assumptions
Synchronization/composition semantics
Environment-conformance obligation
Finite bounds and optional assumption-learning oracle
hooks.exposure_comparison: No compositional proof evaluator is exposed. Per-trace conformance and dependency batching do not discharge environment assumptions or a composition theorem.
hooks.implementation_route: Implement a finite two-component contract checker with separate component and environment results. Add learned assumptions only when a real query oracle exists. Store assumption versions and their source-linked obligations.
focused_acceptance_cases: Components satisfying both obligations compose under the selected rule
An environment that violates the assumption blocks composition
Mutually assumed guarantees without a justified rule are rejected
hooks.falsifier_or_model_defeater: A permitted environment trace violating the assumed protocol defeats the component result's applicability. Passing each component in isolation does not repair this gap.
limits: The cited rule is not permission to use circular reasoning
Unmodeled messages, failures or role changes stay outside coverage
No NASA certification or all-system proof follows from a local adapter

hooks.name: Information-flow / noninterference checks across executions
hooks.mechanism: Compare suitably related executions under an explicit information-flow policy. Vary protected information while preserving the allowed public context, then check the permitted relation on low-observable outputs, including any declared declassification.
proposed_input_contract: Explicit secrecy/visibility policy and allowed declassification
Actor/owner/object identities and roles
Low-equivalent initial-state relation
Paired trace observations with version and environment controls
Observation channel and nondeterminism policy
hooks.exposure_comparison: No dedicated information-flow evaluator is exposed. A generic aligned-field comparison does not define low-equivalence, declassification, or a relation over sets of executions.
hooks.implementation_route: Add a finite paired-trace policy adapter over owned/synthetic account fixtures. Return the first forbidden observable divergence plus its alignment evidence; do not turn sample agreement into universal noninterference.
focused_acceptance_cases: A secret-only variation with equivalent permitted outputs satisfies the sampled obligation
A forbidden output divergence produces the paired witness
An expressly declassified difference is not mislabeled as a violation
hooks.falsifier_or_model_defeater: An authorized public-input difference, permitted declassification, or uncontrolled nondeterminism can defeat an apparent disclosure inference.
limits: Not every hyperproperty reduces to checking one pair of traces
Both accounts must be appropriately authorized for any later live comparison
Timing differences need their own measurement/noise model

hooks.name: NASA event-sequence analysis with common-cause/dependency guards
hooks.mechanism: Starting from a stated initiating event, enumerate modeled success/failure branches through later controls and consequences. Preserve conditional and shared-cause dependencies so apparently redundant controls are not treated as independent evidence.
proposed_input_contract: Initiating event, states and time horizon
Pivotal controls and conditional branch rules
Explicit shared-cause/dependency identities
Mutually exclusive/exhaustive branch assumptions
Outcome definitions; probability inputs only if separately supported
hooks.exposure_comparison: No event-tree/dependency evaluator is exposed. fault_tree is an AND/OR truth evaluator; fmea computes caller-supplied RPN values. Neither establishes dependent-event sequence coverage.
hooks.implementation_route: Implement a qualitative finite branch enumerator and shared-cause guard first. Link each branch to the relevant transition/actor/control atom. Keep probability calculations disabled without a defensible explicit model.
focused_acceptance_cases: A shared credential/provider failure couples two modeled controls
Impossible branch combinations are excluded by explicit conditions
Missing branch/dependency evidence produces incomplete coverage, not an invented likelihood
hooks.falsifier_or_model_defeater: A claimed branch is defeated by an incompatible prerequisite; a redundancy claim is defeated by a documented shared cause. Changing the initiating event changes the question.
limits: This combined hook is one implementation candidate, not two new registered methods
Do not multiply dependent probabilities or manufacture occurrence rates
Qualitative causal paths are model scenarios, not observed incidents

hooks.name: Mechanism-design incentive compatibility
hooks.mechanism: Given an outcome/payment rule, compare an agent's utility under truthful reporting with allowed alternative reports across the declared finite type profiles. Keep incentive, participation and budget constraints separate.
proposed_input_contract: Agents, finite private types and allowed reports
Outcome and transfer rules with source/version
Explicit valuation/cost utility functions
Dominant-strategy versus Bayesian criterion
Outside option, budget policy and any supplied belief distribution
hooks.exposure_comparison: No mechanism-design evaluator is exposed. Nash equilibrium calculation on a supplied matrix and Harsanyi expected utility do not evaluate an allocation/payment mechanism over all declared report/type profiles.
hooks.implementation_route: Add a finite report-deviation inequality checker with separate results for incentive compatibility, individual rationality and any declared budget constraint. Cross-reference an existing game-theory extension if it already provides this operation; do not count it twice.
focused_acceptance_cases: A small truthful fixture has no profitable declared report deviation
A supplied profitable misreport produces its exact type/profile witness
Missing utility or belief inputs stay unresolved instead of becoming zero
hooks.falsifier_or_model_defeater: Changing an assumed utility, allowed report, or policy can defeat the claimed incentive defect. A profitable permitted strategy is not automatically a security vulnerability.
limits: No inferred private beliefs, real-world payoffs, or expected bounty
Checking a fixed mechanism is not synthesizing an optimal mechanism
Bayesian and dominant-strategy conclusions require different inputs and quantifiers

hooks.name: Guarded operation commutativity and distinguishable continuations
hooks.mechanism: Under an explicit precondition, compare admissible operation reorderings using operation-linked responses and the behavior observable after the reordered region. Preserve each actor/thread's own required order. A finite implementation can search for a distinguishing continuation without claiming universal SIM commutativity.
hooks.atomic_operator: Guarded reordering plus comparison of typed observables
proposed_input_contract: Source-bound state and operation IDs, actor/thread identities, object ownership and specification version
An explicit guard saying when the operations may commute and a pure transition/response model
Required per-actor precedence and cross-actor constraints
Exact comparison policy for per-operation responses, ledger entries, authority and final state
Observer model and finite continuation alphabet/depth; any permitted normalization must be justified
Model completeness declarations and separate budgets for reorderings and continuation search

current_mpc_attachment_points.attachment_limits: partial_order validates a supplied order; it does not establish commutativity. Existing metamorphic checks do not prove all reorders or continuations equivalent. Its one-change discipline can represent one explicit order-coordinate variation only if the complete before/after cases are supplied.

hooks.evidence_and_check: Retain both complete histories, operation-to-response pairing, the guard evaluation, model/specification hashes and any distinguishing continuation. Equal aggregate money totals alone do not establish equivalence of owners, beneficiaries, liabilities or future authority.
hooks.implementation_route: A future isolated offline checker could enumerate permitted adjacent swaps or bounded histories, replay a deterministic model, and search bounded continuations. Return COUNTEREXAMPLE, NO_DIFFERENCE_WITHIN_DECLARED_BOUND, INAPPLICABLE or INCONCLUSIVE. Keep the result distinct from linearizability and serializability.
focused_acceptance_cases: Independent updates to different modeled objects commute under the supplied guard, with responses attached to their original operation IDs.
Credit and reset of the same balance produce an explicit order-sensitive counterexample.
Two histories have the same displayed balance but different pending liabilities; a later settle operation distinguishes them.
A guard that fails makes the proposed commutation inapplicable; it does not label the specified order dependence a vulnerability.
A budget limit or incomplete continuation model remains inconclusive, never universally commutative.
hooks.falsifier_or_model_defeater: One valid distinguishing result or continuation defeats the asserted commutativity for that state and guard. Missing model state, inappropriate observable normalization or an unjustified guard defeats applicability. A lawful order-sensitive operation is not automatically a defect.
limits: A finite reorder comparison is weaker than the paper's quantified SI/SIM definitions.
Pairwise observed equality does not establish all multi-operation reorderings or future histories.
Commutativity is distinct from idempotency: repeating one operation is a separate obligation.
No guarantee of multicore scalability, exploitability, target correctness or authorization follows from this proposed check.
This subtask supplies a research contract only; no checker or target interaction was executed.

hooks.name: Finite evidence-view knowledge checking
hooks.mechanism: Evaluate whether an asserted fact is true at every modeled point that an actor cannot distinguish using its declared view. A point with the same view and a false fact is a concrete countermodel to a knowledge assertion even when the fact happens to be true at the actual point.
hooks.atomic_operator: Counterworld construction plus finite universal checking over a view equivalence class
proposed_input_contract: Finite model points with stable IDs, provenance and explicit actual-point selection
Actor/service identities and an exact view function based only on information they can observe
Typed ground facts per point; unknown truth values remain unknown
The proposition, any allowed Boolean structure, and the knowledge operator being tested
Model-world completeness and observation completeness declarations
If group operators are requested, exact group membership and a distinct operator for everyone, distributed or common knowledge

current_mpc_attachment_points.attachment_limits: Existing identity and authority graphs can supply source-bound participants and information boundaries. Harsanyi models supplied types/payoffs; it is not this modal-knowledge checker. ACH can retain the alternative world as a competing explanation but does not execute epistemic semantics.

hooks.evidence_and_check: Retain the actual point and counterworld IDs, identical view projections, conflicting proposition values, excluded observations and the model's assumptions. Use this to test unsupported promotions such as 'the client observed success, therefore the authority finalized payment'.
hooks.implementation_route: A future isolated offline checker could partition finite points by canonical typed views and evaluate the proposition on each relevant class. It must distinguish FACT_TRUE, KNOWLEDGE_HOLDS_IN_SUPPLIED_MODEL, COUNTERWORLD_FOUND and INCONCLUSIVE. Optional group extensions require separate documented semantics; no bisimulation solver is implied.
focused_acceptance_cases: Pending and committed states expose the same client view; finality is true at only one, so the checker returns the other as a counterworld.
A newly verified authoritative receipt separates those two modeled views, changing the finite knowledge result only if its authenticity and meaning are established outside this checker.
A false fact at the actual point cannot be reported as known when actual-point membership is enforced.
Removing a contrary world without evidence does not improve real-world certainty; a completeness downgrade must propagate.
Missing point valuation or observation provenance yields an unknown result instead of false certainty.
Numeric identity 7 and text identity '7' remain different when constructing views; lossy normalization cannot erase an information boundary.
hooks.falsifier_or_model_defeater: One admissible counterworld with the same actor view defeats knowledge of the fact in that model. Conversely, proving that the counterworld is unreachable or that the actor can distinguish it may defeat that counterexample, with explicit evidence.
limits: Finite supplied worlds do not establish that all real-world possibilities were represented.
Knowledge in this formal sense is relative to a view and model; it does not certify human awareness, belief, honesty or computational ability.
Unknown evidence authenticity cannot become trusted merely because the view includes a receipt-shaped object.
Every actor knowing a fact, joint evidence determining it and common knowledge are distinct operators.
This is separate from information-flow noninterference, which compares trace sets under a secrecy policy.
This subtask supplies a research contract only; no checker, classifier promotion or target request was executed.
